summary: Steffen Döll works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an M.A. (1998–2004) and doctorate (~2004–2009) at the University of Munich. In 2015, he was appointed Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg.

Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian who completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919) under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held posts at Visva-Bharati (1922–1950), Calcutta (1924–1950), and Pennsylvania (1950–1993).

Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Oslo, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg (doctorate ~1891–1893 under Richard Pischel). He was a professor at Oslo (1910–1937) and Hamburg (1914–1919).
Stephan Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy, earning degrees from Oberlin, Stanford, UCSC, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She was a professor at Vermont (1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctoral work at Yale (~1972–1977) under Stanley Insler. She taught at Harvard and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in ~2002.

Stephen A. Murphy works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London, where he also pursued doctoral studies under Elizabeth H. Moore.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan (1971–1977). He served as professor of art history at Kansas (1977–1992) and Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied with teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He directed Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and later joined the faculty of Bodhi College (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held a Fulbright fellowship at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997). He serves as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University (attested 2013).

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who earned his bachelor's from Oberlin and master's and doctorate from Princeton (~1979–1986). In ~1996, he became D. T. Suzuki Professor at Princeton.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a Ph.D. at Vienna (~1948–1950). He founded the Anthropos Institute (1950) and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954).

Stephen G. Covell specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and held a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

Stephen G. Williams is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford and earned an MA from Colorado State University (~2016–2018) under Andre Archie, later holding a post at Worcester College, Oxford.
Stephen H. Phillips is a philosopher and Indologist who served as professor of philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 1999) and later became Professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Stephen Harris is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of New Mexico by 2014 and became University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Stephen J. Laumakis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West. He serves as Professor of Philosophy at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctorate at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).
